The baritone horn is a B♭ piston-valve brass instrument of the saxhorn family, Hornbostel–Sachs 423.232. It sounds with the lips and commonly has three or four piston valves; central and eastern Europe mostly use rotary valves, where the instrument is called the Tenorhorn. The bore is moderately conical and narrower than the euphonium's, and it uses a wide-rimmed cup mouthpiece. It is used mainly in brass bands, military music and concert bands; the standard British brass band has two, and parts marked baritone in American concert bands are usually played on the euphonium, which can also play the trombone part.
